chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali al-Sa'i, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, I used to practice Mut'ah (temporary marriage), but I disliked it and took it as an ill omen, so I gave God a pledge between the Corner and the Station (in Mecca), and made a vow and fasting upon that that I would not marry (via Mut'ah). Then that became difficult for me, and I regretted my oath, but I have the strength in my hand to marry (via Mut'ah) openly.' He said to me, 'You pledged to God that you would not obey Him, and by God, if you do not obey Him, you will definitely disobey Him.'
And dislike (for Mut'ah) has been reported for that day because of the increase in confidence in women on that day.

key_terms.بَيْنَ الرُّكْنِ وَالْمَقَامِ: Between the Corner and the Station (a specific location in Mecca for making vows)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking a vow to abstain from temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of *Nadhr al-Ta'ah* (vow of obedience) when one vows to abstain from a permissible act like Mut'ah; the Imam explains that such a vow is essentially a command to obey God, so breaking it constitutes disobedience. Historically, this addresses the specific context of the day when trust in women was perceived as high, providing a nuanced view on the social utility of temporary marriage. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that a vow to refrain from a *Mubah* (permissible) act transforms it into an obligatory duty for the vower.
